exercises.passage:
The Lantern Festival falls on the 15th day of the first month of the lunar calendar. Ancient people also called it the Shangyuan Festival. Celebrations and traditions on this day began from the Han Dynasty and became popular in the Sui and Tang Dynasties.

Watching the red lanterns is one of the main traditions. Lanterns of different shapes and sizes are usually hung on trees or along river banks on show. It is said that sky lanterns were first used by Zhuge Kongming to ask for help when he was in trouble. Today, when the lanterns slowly rise into the air, people make wishes.

Another tradition is guessing lantern riddles (谜语). The riddles are usually short, wise, and sometimes humorous. The answer to a riddle can be a Chinese character (汉字), a famous person's name, or a place's name.

The most important thing is to eat sweet dumplings with different tastes. In northern China, they are called yuanxiao while in southern parts they're named tangyuan. Making sweet dumplings is like a game or an activity, so they are usually done happily by a group of friends or family members.

In old times, the Lantern Festival was also "romantic*". Watching lanterns gave young people a chance to meet each other. A line from Xin Qiji, a poet during the Song Dynasty, shows this:
But in the crowd once and again, I look for her in vain. When all at once I turn my head, I find her there where lantern lights are dimly shed.
* The word "romantic" means connected or concerned with love.

From April 12 to 15 this year, the Dai people celebrated their biggest event: the Water-Splashing Festival.

There are more than one million Dai people in China. Most of them live in Yunnan Province. They hold the festival every year for three to seven days in mid-April. __7__

The tradition of water splashing began in Persia in the fifth century. __8__ Later, it gradually became a folk tradition of the Dai people. The festival is also widely celebrated in Thailand, Laos and some other Asian countries.

__9__ They also hold activities of celebration. Many people send out burning lanterns into the sky. They sing and dance in the streets. And colorful dragon boat races take place on the Lancang River.

The most exciting moment of the festival is, of course, water splashing. People first go to temples and wash Buddha statues (佛像) with clean water. After that, the joyful and messy water splashing begins. People use all kinds of containers (容器) to hold water. They flood the streets to chase and play with each other.

__10__ Splashing water expresses wishes to wash away illness and disaster. The wetter one gets, the more wishes he receives.

exercises.passage:
In a small town, there was a big event every year called the Grape Festival. This year, a young girl named Mia decided to join in. She wanted to do more than just watch this time.

On the festival day, the town square was full of colors and happy sounds. There were shops selling grapes and grape foods. Music played, and kids ran around. Mia wore her purple dress and brought her grape cake to the festival. She was a bit scared but very excited.

First, Mia watched the grape stomping (踩). People stood in big boxes and stepped heavily on grapes with their feet to see who could do it the fastest. It looked fun and exciting. Mia cheered for them in the crowd. Then, there was the wine tasting. Grown-ups tried different wines and talked about them. Mia was too young to taste them, but she liked seeing everyone talking happily. Finally, it was time for the competition for the best grape dessert. Mia was very nervous. When the judges (裁判) tasted her cake, they smiled. Mia felt hopeful. In the end, Mia's cake won second place! She was so happy and proud.

The festival ended with a big parade (游行). There were cars dressed up with grapes, painted with deep purples and light greens, passing the joy of the grape harvest. Children danced along, trying to catch the grape candies thrown into the crowd, while the air was filled with laughter around the whole town.

This festival was about more than just grapes. It was a time for the town to come together, and make happy memories. For Mia, it was a very special day. She had tried something new and found out how great it felt to join in and do well.

Father's Day in 2024 was on June 16. The world's first Father's Day was in 1910 in the United States. Now, many countries, like the US, Canada, and China, celebrate it on the third Sunday of June. On this day, people give gifts to their dads or spend time with them. __14__

In Germany, fathers get Father's Day off work. This fun-filled day falls on a Thursday in May. It's said that in the past, the father with the most children in the village would get a reward. __15__ Fathers often spend the day with their friends who are also fathers. Some of the most popular activities include bike tours and park parties to play games.

Australians celebrate Father's Day on the first Sunday in September. The first Father's Day celebration was in the 1930s. It became popular in the 1960s. __16__ Children can buy gifts like cups and socks for their fathers at school on Father's Day.

__17__ People also celebrate the birth anniversary of the country's longest-serving (在位时间最长的) king on this day. The people show respect for their fathers and grandfathers by giving them a canna (美人蕉) flower. Bangkok, the capital of Thailand, allows fathers to take the bus or subway for free. __18__ This is meant to encourage families to spend time together.

exercises.sample_essay:
The Spring Festival is one of the most important traditional festivals in China. It usually comes in January or February.
Before the festival, people usually clean their houses because they think cleaning can sweep away bad luck. They also prepare lots of delicious food and drinks.
On the eve of the festival, family members get together and have a big dinner. They enjoy different kinds of food such as dumplings and fish. Then they watch the Spring Festival Gala on TV.
During the festival, people wear new clothes and visit their relatives and friends. They say "Happy Chinese New Year" to each other. Children get red packets from the old.

exercises.stem: 在中国悠久的历史长河中，传统节日如颗颗明珠，串联起民族的记忆与情感。春节的喜庆鞭炮、端午的香甜粽子、中秋的皎洁月光……每一个传统节日都散发着独特的魅力。请写一篇短文，介绍你最喜欢的中国传统节日，并阐述你上次是如何庆祝它的以及你的感受。
